It leaves Ollama enabled at the default loopback address. Two positive cases and two disabled-default cases call `container.start()`. On these fresh fixtures, that service reads its enabled default, uses the process fetch implementation and requests `/api/tags` at `127.0.0.1:11434`. A responding endpoint with installed models can trigger version and per-model metadata requests. The ordinary test setup configures API port allocation. [New environment](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794/apps/api/src/preflight-catalog.test.ts#L39) · [Positive starts](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794/apps/api/src/preflight-catalog.test.ts#L133) · [Disabled starts](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794/apps/api/src/preflight-catalog.test.ts#L265) · [Ollama defaults](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794/apps/api/src/config.ts#L36) · [Container startup](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794/apps/api/src/container.ts#L560) · [Discovery](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794/packages/infrastructure/src/ollama/discovery.ts#L80)

This entire test file is absent at both the runtime parent and target main. Existing tests also use the service. The independent QA guard recorded ten blocked requests during a three-file suite, six from one worker and four from another. The guard records no test filename or stack. The new source establishes the introduced reachability independently of request-by-request attribution. Set `GG_OLLAMA_ENABLED` to `false` in the test’s own environment or inject an isolated service. Verify the single file through its ordinary test entry point with an outbound observer, retaining startup and catalog assertions and expecting zero requests to the host endpoint. # Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

# #448 D194 independent corrective QA: plan

Written 2026-11-21 before any execution, checkout change or driver run. Role: actual Claude Opus 5.5/xhigh behaviour QA, separate from the GPT author (`i4-448-test-author-01`) and Fable corrective review (`i4-448-test-fable-review-01`, running concurrently against the read-only author checkout). The scope is the corrected test file only. This is not a general review.

## Inputs read

- D194 (`decision-194.md`, `d194-catalog-entry.json`), final scan 3 report (`i4-551-final-astra-01/report.md`), author report (`i4-448-test-author-01/report.md`) and root freeze (`i4-448-test-root-freeze-01/receipt.json`).
- Brief SHA-256 `05344da2…d1a5` and spec SHA-256 `787bde5a…d915` were verified before planning. `BRIEF.md`, `spec.json` and `provider/` are read-only.

## Binding (verified read-only before planning)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate | `446da9ce32b2304f17c53b5ff09af559f35dd3cf` |
| Tree / parent | `53af267660277933a2dd57718b528b7849cea2fb` / `cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794` |
| Delta | `apps/api/src/preflight-catalog.test.ts` only, 128 insertions and 5 deletions. Blob `a187acae…`, SHA-256 `a67356cd…611ae` |
| QA checkout | `G:/ggq/gg-i4-448-qa/GraphGoblin`. Branch `codex/gg-i4-448-qa` at `b45807f0`. No tracked or untracked changes; only ignored build/install output. No foreign process references it |

| Runtime | Node `v22.23.4` from `C:/Users/98jak/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64`, first on PATH. `C:/nvm4w/nodejs/pnpm.cmd` 12.8.1 matches `packageManager`, so pnpm will not switch versions |

## Step 0: bind the checkout (authorized)

1. Record the branch, HEAD, status and worktree git directory. Stop and report to root if the checkout is dirty.
2. Run `git -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false fetch --no-auto-gc --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules --no-write-commit-graph G:/ggq/gg-i4-448-preflight/GraphGoblin codex/gg-i4-448-preflight` with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. Verify that FETCH_HEAD is the candidate. The shared object store already holds the commit. Automatic GC is disabled so the shared repository is not repacked.
3. Run `git checkout --detach 446da9ce…`. Verify HEAD, tree, file SHA-256, a clean status and that branch `codex/gg-i4-448-qa` still points to `b45807f0`. Do not move or delete it.
4. Read the author checkout's HEAD and status only, with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, before and after the QA work.

## Instrumentation (own drivers in `driver/`; never in the repo)

- **Guard `guard.cjs`**, loaded by `NODE_OPTIONS=--require`, so every Node process in the tree inherits it, including Vitest's forks. It has two independent layers. Every event is appended synchronously because Vitest kills its fork without exit hooks.
  - **L1, API layer.** It wraps `globalThis.fetch`, `net.Socket.prototype.connect`, `http/https.request|get`, `tls.connect`, `dns.lookup`, `dns.promises.lookup`, `dns.resolve*` and `dgram` `send`/`connect`. It records the target and stack, then rejects synchronously before the original is called. Non-network behaviour passes through and is counted: `data:`/`blob:` fetch, path-based IPC/named-pipe `connect`, `listen`, filesystem and child processes.
  - **L2, handle layer**, if the capability probe confirms it. It wraps `process.binding('tcp_wrap').TCP.prototype.connect/connect6`, `udp_wrap` send and `cares_wrap.getaddrinfo`. These are the libuv/c-ares entry points below L1, and they return a UV error before any socket or resolver traffic occurs. L2 is proven separately with L1 disabled.
  - **Observers (passive).** One records each `lstat` of `<fixture>/data/chat-audio`. Only `container.start()` reaches that call, through `cleanupAudio(true)`, immediately before `ollama.start()`; this counts actual startup paths. Another takes synchronous independent snapshots (`readdirSync`, `statSync`, SHA-256 and SQLite header fields) of `gg-preflight-catalog-*` fixture directories whenever the test lists them and before its `afterEach` `rm`. These snapshots include `-shm`, which the helper ignores.
- **OS observer `tcp-poll.ps1`, native and supplementary.** It polls `Get-NetTCPConnection` every 250 ms and the driver's descendant PID set every second. It records any TCP row owned by that process tree, including pnpm.exe, which the Node guard cannot cover. DNS through the Windows DNS client service is not visible at this layer; L1 and L2 cover it.
- **Runner `run-command.ps1`.** It writes per-command stdout, stderr, the exact argv, environment deltas and a receipt with timestamps, exit code and node path/version. It records the candidate file SHA-256 before and after and the `git status` before and after. A receipt is never overwritten. `npm_config_update_notifier=false` is set per process so pnpm makes no update check.
- **SQLite driver `sqlite-qa.mts`.** It runs under `node --conditions=development --import tsx` with cwd `apps/api` and imports the production TypeScript through absolute file URLs. Nothing is placed in the repo. It is my own fixture design.
  - Each store is built by the production `openDatabase().migrate()` and `SqliteModelCatalog.seed()` in a **separate child process that exits**. Process exit releases every native handle, which avoids the finalizer race without copying. The driver then verifies the WAL-mode header (bytes 18/19 = 2) and the directory listing.
  - Real `runPreflightCli` runs in a child process under the guard. Observations are taken **before**, **immediately after** in the child and **settled** after child exit. Each records the listing, sizes, SHA-256, DB header, WAL header and frame count. Catalog and `__drizzle_migrations` rows are read by Node's bundled `node:sqlite`, a different SQLite build from the product's libsql, from snapshot copies so the reader cannot alter the observed files.
  - Real frames come from `node:sqlite` writers with `wal_autocheckpoint=0`.
  - The candidate helper is executed **verbatim**. Lines 73–103 (`storeBytes`, `expectStoreUnchanged`) are sliced from the frozen Git blob, hash-verified, and run with Vitest's real `expect`. The old predicate is the parent's verbatim `expect(await storeBytes(dbFile)).toEqual(before)`. My own contract predicate is derived from D194 and is independent of both.

## Runs (finite; at most 3 driver iterations for distinct instrumentation fixes)

| # | Run | Class | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 00 | Capability probes: process.binding availability, `node:sqlite`, tsx import, standalone Vitest `expect` | probe | Recorded; it determines whether L2 is enabled |
| 01 | Guard self-check: deliberate fetch, http, net, tls, dns and dgram attempts at 127.0.0.1:9, `localhost` and a `.invalid` name, from the parent and a forked child. Repeated with L1 disabled to prove L2. Forwarding checks cover `data:` fetch and named-pipe IPC | controlled | Every attempt is recorded and blocked. Forwarded operations succeed. No OS TCP rows |
| 02 | Product-path control: `createContainer(...).start()` on my fixture with `GG_OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9`, Ollama default **enabled**, then with the candidate's `GG_OLLAMA_ENABLED=false` | controlled | Enabled: at least one blocked `/api/tags` attempt with a discovery stack. Disabled: zero. Port 11434 is never targeted |
| 03 | **Ordinary isolated file**: `pnpm.cmd --filter @graphgoblin/api test src/preflight-catalog.test.ts --reporter=verbose` plus JSON output, with the guard, observers and OS poll | native, instrumented | 14/14 pass. Zero blocked attempts in every process. Installation is logged in the Vitest parent and fork. Exactly four `start()` `chat-audio` probes. Independent snapshots satisfy D194 for each case |

# #448 D194 independent corrective QA: plan

Written 2026-11-21 before any execution, checkout change or driver run. Role: actual Claude Opus 5.5/xhigh behaviour QA, separate from the GPT author (`i4-448-test-author-01`) and Fable corrective review (`i4-448-test-fable-review-01`, running concurrently against the read-only author checkout). The scope is the corrected test file only. This is not a general review.

## Inputs read

- D194 (`decision-194.md`, `d194-catalog-entry.json`), final scan 3 report (`i4-551-final-astra-01/report.md`), author report (`i4-448-test-author-01/report.md`) and root freeze (`i4-448-test-root-freeze-01/receipt.json`).
- Brief SHA-256 `05344da2…d1a5` and spec SHA-256 `787bde5a…d915` were verified before planning. `BRIEF.md`, `spec.json` and `provider/` are read-only.

## Binding (verified read-only before planning)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate | `446da9ce32b2304f17c53b5ff09af559f35dd3cf` |
| Tree / parent | `53af267660277933a2dd57718b528b7849cea2fb` / `cc0a52cffe7e0bffb197c3f3342d370e2b1b9794` |
| Delta | `apps/api/src/preflight-catalog.test.ts` only, 128 insertions and 5 deletions. Blob `a187acae…`, SHA-256 `a67356cd…611ae` |
| QA checkout | `G:/ggq/gg-i4-448-qa/GraphGoblin`. Branch `codex/gg-i4-448-qa` at `b45807f0`. No tracked or untracked changes; only ignored build/install output. No foreign process references it |

| Runtime | Node `v22.23.4` from `C:/Users/98jak/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64`, first on PATH. `C:/nvm4w/nodejs/pnpm.cmd` 12.8.1 matches `packageManager`, so pnpm will not switch versions |
| TEMP/TMP | `G:/ggq/qa-scratch/i4-448-test-independent-01`. Its existing `claude/` subfolder is not mine and will not be touched |

## Step 0: bind the checkout (authorized)

1. Record the branch, HEAD, status and worktree git directory. Stop and report to root if the checkout is dirty.
2. Run `git -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false fetch --no-auto-gc --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules --no-write-commit-graph G:/ggq/gg-i4-448-preflight/GraphGoblin codex/gg-i4-448-preflight` with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. Verify that FETCH_HEAD is the candidate. The shared object store already holds the commit. Automatic GC is disabled so the shared repository is not repacked.
3. Run `git checkout --detach 446da9ce…`. Verify HEAD, tree, file SHA-256, a clean status and that branch `codex/gg-i4-448-qa` still points to `b45807f0`. Do not move or delete it.
4. Read the author checkout's HEAD and status only, with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, before and after the QA work.

## Instrumentation (own drivers in `driver/`; never in the repo)

- **Guard `guard.cjs`**, loaded by `NODE_OPTIONS=--require`, so every Node process in the tree inherits it, including Vitest's forks. It has two independent layers. Every event is appended synchronously because Vitest kills its fork without exit hooks.
  - **L1, API layer.** It wraps `globalThis.fetch`, `net.Socket.prototype.connect`, `http/https.request|get`, `tls.connect`, `dns.lookup`, `dns.promises.lookup`, `dns.resolve*` and `dgram` `send`/`connect`. It records the target and stack, then rejects synchronously before the original is called. Non-network behaviour passes through and is counted: `data:`/`blob:` fetch, path-based IPC/named-pipe `connect`, `listen`, filesystem and child processes.
  - **L2, handle layer**, if the capability probe confirms it. It wraps `process.binding('tcp_wrap').TCP.prototype.connect/connect6`, `udp_wrap` send and `cares_wrap.getaddrinfo`. These are the libuv/c-ares entry points below L1, and they return a UV error before any socket or resolver traffic occurs. L2 is proven separately with L1 disabled.
  - **Observers (passive).** One records each `lstat` of `<fixture>/data/chat-audio`. Only `container.start()` reaches that call, through `cleanupAudio(true)`, immediately before `ollama.start()`; this counts actual startup paths. Another takes synchronous independent snapshots (`readdirSync`, `statSync`, SHA-256 and SQLite header fields) of `gg-preflight-catalog-*` fixture directories whenever the test lists them and before its `afterEach` `rm`. These snapshots include `-shm`, which the helper ignores.
- **OS observer `tcp-poll.ps1`, native and supplementary.** It polls `Get-NetTCPConnection` every 250 ms and the driver's descendant PID set every second. It records any TCP row owned by that process tree, including pnpm.exe, which the Node guard cannot cover. DNS through the Windows DNS client service is not visible at this layer; L1 and L2 cover it.
- **Runner `run-command.ps1`.** It writes per-command stdout, stderr, the exact argv, environment deltas and a receipt with timestamps, exit code and node path/version. It records the candidate file SHA-256 before and after and the `git status` before and after. A receipt is never overwritten. `npm_config_update_notifier=false` is set per process so pnpm makes no update check.
- **SQLite driver `sqlite-qa.mts`.** It runs under `node --conditions=development --import tsx` with cwd `apps/api` and imports the production TypeScript through absolute file URLs. Nothing is placed in the repo. It is my own fixture design.
  - Each store is built by the production `openDatabase().migrate()` and `SqliteModelCatalog.seed()` in a **separate child process that exits**. Process exit releases every native handle, which avoids the finalizer race without copying. The driver then verifies the WAL-mode header (bytes 18/19 = 2) and the directory listing.
  - Real `runPreflightCli` runs in a child process under the guard. Observations are taken **before**, **immediately after** in the child and **settled** after child exit. Each records the listing, sizes, SHA-256, DB header, WAL header and frame count. Catalog and `__drizzle_migrations` rows are read by Node's bundled `node:sqlite`, a different SQLite build from the product's libsql, from snapshot copies so the reader cannot alter the observed files.
  - Real frames come from `node:sqlite` writers with `wal_autocheckpoint=0`.
  - The candidate helper is executed **verbatim**. Lines 73–103 (`storeBytes`, `expectStoreUnchanged`) are sliced from the frozen Git blob, hash-verified, and run with Vitest's real `expect`. The old predicate is the parent's verbatim `expect(await storeBytes(dbFile)).toEqual(before)`. My own contract predicate is derived from D194 and is independent of both.

## Runs (finite; at most 3 driver iterations for distinct instrumentation fixes)

| # | Run | Class | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 00 | Capability probes: process.binding availability, `node:sqlite`, tsx import, standalone Vitest `expect` | probe | Recorded; it determines whether L2 is enabled |
| 01 | Guard self-check: deliberate fetch, http, net, tls, dns and dgram attempts at 127.0.0.1:9, `localhost` and a `.invalid` name, from the parent and a forked child. Repeated with L1 disabled to prove L2. Forwarding checks cover `data:` fetch and named-pipe IPC | controlled | Every attempt is recorded and blocked. Forwarded operations succeed. No OS TCP rows |
| 02 | Product-path control: `createContainer(...).start()` on my fixture with `GG_OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9`, Ollama default **enabled**, then with the candidate's `GG_OLLAMA_ENABLED=false` | controlled | Enabled: at least one blocked `/api/tags` attempt with a discovery stack. Disabled: zero. Port 11434 is never targeted |
| 03 | **Ordinary isolated file**: `pnpm.cmd --filter @graphgoblin/api test src/preflight-catalog.test.ts --reporter=verbose` plus JSON output, with the guard, observers and OS poll | native, instrumented | 14/14 pass. Zero blocked attempts in every process. Installation is logged in the Vitest parent and fork. Exactly four `start()` `chat-audio` probes. Independent snapshots satisfy D194 for each case |
| 04 | SQLite scenarios S1 verified-absent, S2 pre-existing empty and S3 frozen nonempty WAL, with real preflight | native product, controlled fixture | DB bytes identical. Rows and migrations are unchanged. S2/S3 WAL is present and identical. S1 WAL is absent or exactly empty; the actual state is reported |
| 04 | Observer control matrix on real files, in the same driver | controlled | Accepts: unchanged absent, absent→empty, empty→empty, nonempty unchanged with `-shm` change. Rejects: DB byte flip, real checkpoint into the DB, DB removal, empty WAL removed, real frames on absent/empty WAL, nonempty WAL byte change, removal, truncation and appended real frame, and a 32-byte header-only WAL |
| 05 | Old-predicate control against S1 observations reloaded from saved, hash-verified blobs | controlled | The old strict predicate rejects only when the absent→empty transition was actually observed. The candidate helper accepts. If S1 stays absent on this host, this is reported and not inferred |
| 06 | Post-checks: checkout status, file hash and branch, author checkout HEAD/status, process absence, owned scratch, retained SQLite blobs | check | Clean, unchanged and absent |
| 07 | Seal: SHA-256 of every file I wrote | seal | — |

Not run, per the brief: the historical 61-test or broad suites, the author's mutation experiments, typecheck/lint (already passing), browser, real provider or CLI, GitHub, and ports 4747/4748/11434. The historical ten requests from three files are not attributed to this file.

## Criteria and verdict rules

- **C1, isolation.** PASS requires: run 01 proves blocking on both layers; run 02 proves sensitivity to the actual F1 path and that the `false` setting closes it; run 03 records zero attempts and exactly four startup paths, with all 14 tests passing. Any attempt in run 03, or any of the four startups missing, is a FAIL. An instrumentation gap I cannot close is CONDITIONAL.
- **C2, storage contract.** PASS requires both real-preflight scenarios and run 03's independent snapshots to satisfy D194, and every matrix control to give the expected decision from both the verbatim helper and my predicate. A decision mismatch is a FAIL with the exact case.
- **C3, old-predicate control.** PASS requires the strict predicate to reject the actually observed absent→empty transition and the helper to accept it. If the transition is not observed natively, the result is CONDITIONAL and recorded factually.
- **C4, scope and preservation.** PASS requires the checkout to be clean at the candidate after QA. The source, the author checkout and the sealed evidence must be unchanged, with no owned processes left behind.

# #448 D194 independent corrective QA: report

**Verdict: PASS for the corrected test file, by all four criteria.** The limits are listed below. This is the separate Claude Opus 5.5/xhigh behaviour QA; it is neither the author's run nor the Fable review. Only the test-only correction was assessed. Hosted CI at the exact head and current target, canonical native verification, root/coordinator completion and the owner-only #448 closure remain open. This QA does not complete them.

| Criterion | Result | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1: the isolated file makes no outbound attempts; four startup paths are retained | **PASS** | Deliberate attempts are blocked by each guard layer alone (01c, 01d). The real F1 discovery path is caught when Ollama is enabled and absent with the candidate setting (02a/02b). The ordinary file run records 0 attempts in two replicates (03a/03b). There are exactly 4 `container.start()` paths (03b) |
| C2: D194 storage contract on genuine SQLite files | **PASS** | Independent before/after snapshots of the actual candidate run show absent→0 B, 0 B→0 B and frozen 8,272 B→identical (03b). My real-preflight scenarios S1/S2a/S2b/S3 match the contract (04). The verbatim helper agrees with my predicate on 19/19 real-file controls, including real SQLite frames and checkpoints (04) |
| C3: the original strict predicate rejects the observed absent→empty transition | **PASS** | The parent's verbatim statement rejects 4/4 captured absent→0 B transitions: 2 from S1 and 2 from the actual candidate test run. It accepts 6/6 unchanged cases. The candidate helper accepts all 10 (05) |
| C4: scope, preservation and cleanup | **PASS** | The checkout is clean and detached at the candidate, with its prior branch preserved. The author checkout is unchanged. Both original seals re-verify. No owned process remains. Owned scratch was removed after inventory (06/06b) |

## Binding

- **Candidate.** `446da9ce32b2304f17c53b5ff09af559f35dd3cf`, tree `53af2676…`, parent `cc0a52cf…`. The only delta is `apps/api/src/preflight-catalog.test.ts`: blob `a187acae…`, SHA-256 `a67356cd6773b265df80ced4e26a9c1f17cd0fe0c48f2d4cb286ddc315c611ae`. The parent blob `582e28ee…` has SHA-256 `14b1532e…4b71`.
- **QA checkout** `G:/ggq/gg-i4-448-qa/GraphGoblin`.
  - Before: clean on `codex/gg-i4-448-qa` at `b45807f0`. Only ignored build/install output was present, and no foreign process referenced it.
  - Steps: I fetched `codex/gg-i4-448-preflight` from the read-only author checkout with automatic GC and maintenance disabled. FETCH_HEAD was the candidate, and I then ran `checkout --detach`.
  - After: HEAD, tree, parent and file hash are verified. Status and index are empty. Branch `codex/gg-i4-448-qa` is still at `b45807f0` (`commands/00a–00c`, with an erratum noted below).
- **Dependencies.** No package, lockfile or config path differs between `b45807f0` and the candidate. The existing install was reused and nothing was installed.
- **Runtime.**
  - Node `v22.23.4` from the project runtime, first on PATH.
  - `C:/nvm4w/nodejs/pnpm.cmd` 12.8.1, which matches `packageManager`.
  - Vitest 5.0.3 and tsx 4.23.15.
  - TEMP/TMP `G:/ggq/qa-scratch/i4-448-test-independent-01`.
  - `npm_config_update_notifier=false` was set per process.
  - No `GG_*` variables were inherited.

## C1: isolation of the new file

**Instrumentation** (`driver/v2/guard.cjs`, loaded by `NODE_OPTIONS=--require` into every Node process and Vitest fork). Each event is appended synchronously.

- **L1, API layer.** It covers fetch, WebSocket/EventSource, `net.Socket#connect`, http/https/tls, dns and dgram. Each is rejected before the original is called. IPC/named pipes, `data:` fetch, IP-literal `lookup`, `listen`, filesystem access and child processes are passed through and counted.
- **L2, handle layer.** `process.binding` `tcp_wrap` connect/connect6, `udp_wrap` send/connect and `cares_wrap` getaddrinfo/queries return `UV_EACCES`.
- **Native, supplementary.** `tcp-poll.ps1` records every TCP row and UDP endpoint owned by the runner's descendants.

Results:

- **01c (L1+L2) and 01d (L2 only), controlled.** All seven deliberate attempt types were rejected: fetch, `http.get`, `net.connect`, `tls.connect`, `dns.lookup`, `dns.promises.lookup` and UDP send. This held in the parent and in a forked child, whose guard was inherited. In-process TCP and UDP honeypots accepted 0 connections and received 0 datagrams. The forwarding checks for `data:` fetch and named-pipe round trips succeeded. In 01d, L1 was disabled and every attempt failed with `EACCES` at the libuv/c-ares layer, so each layer blocks on its own.
- **02a, controlled: real F1 path with Ollama enabled.** This used the parent commit's environment shape with `GG_OLLAMA_URL` pointed at my honeypot, so port 11434 was never targeted. `createContainer(...).start()` produced exactly one blocked `GET http://127.0.0.1:50396/api/tags`, 86 ms after start. Its stack is `ollama/http.ts:66` ← `discovery.ts:80` ← `services.ts:74/100/154`. The honeypot accepted 0 connections. The poller recorded the honeypot's LISTEN row, which shows it can see sockets owned by the process tree.
- **02b, controlled: `GG_OLLAMA_ENABLED='false'`.** The config read `ollamaEnabled:false`. There were 0 attempts over the full 6 s wait after start plus 0.5 s, and 0 honeypot connections.
- **03a, native, guard only.** The ordinary single-file command passed **14/14** in 10.80 s with exit code 0.
  - The guard was installed in the Vitest parent (PID 12608) and its fork (13340, child of 12608). Both recorded **0 blocked and 0 attempted** operations.
  - The poller tracked cmd, pnpm.exe, the node parent and fork, and the product's lock-check PowerShell and conhost. It took 19 samples and found **0 TCP or UDP rows**.
- **03b, native, guard plus passive observers.** It passed **14/14** with **0 attempts** and 0 TCP/UDP rows.
  - `startup-chat-audio-probe` fired **exactly 4 times**. Each came from `chat-audio.ts:213` ← `container.ts:267` ← `container.ts:559`. Line 559 is `await cleanupAudio(true)`, inside `start()` and immediately before `ollama.start()` on line 560.
  - Two came from test line 160 (positive codex and claude starts) and two from test line 292 (disabled codex WARN and claude FAIL starts). The refusal cases did not start.
- The historical ten requests came from a different three-file run. They are not attributed to this file, and that run was not repeated.

## C2: storage contract on genuine SQLite files

**In the actual candidate run (03b, native).** My observer took 60 independent synchronous snapshots (`readdirSync`, sizes, SHA-256, DB header and WAL parse with checksum validation), including `-shm`. All 81 helper reads byte-match the independent snapshot taken at the same moment.

| Candidate test (fixture) | Before | After preflight and reads | My predicate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| initially absent WAL (`xDeZzo`) | DB `c749672c…` only; **no `-wal`, no `-shm`** | DB identical; **`-wal` 0 B** + 32 KiB `-shm` created (2 samples) | accept |
| initially empty WAL (`mgEqiU`) | DB `c749672c…`, `-wal` 0 B, no `-shm` | DB identical, `-wal` 0 B, `-shm` created | accept |
| WAL-backed store (`UYpKlA`) | DB `7bd5d622…`, `-wal` 8,272 B (2 frames, both checksum-valid, 1 commit) | DB and WAL byte-identical; `-shm` changed | accept |
| tests 1–10 | DB plus a pre-existing 0 B `-wal` and `-shm` (left by the in-process `fixture()`) | unchanged | accept for every sample |

On the negative-control test (`ECME4W`), my predicate agrees with all 8 designed transitions. It rejects the DB byte flip, the removed empty WAL, real frames on an absent or empty WAL, a WAL byte flip, WAL removal and truncation to 0, and it accepts absent→empty. My parser independently found that the flipped WAL's checksum-valid frame prefix fell from 2 to 1.

**My independent real-preflight scenarios (04, native product code and real SQLite, with fixtures I controlled).** Each store was built by the production writer in a child process that exited. The real `runPreflightCli` ran in its own child process. Observations were taken before, immediately after (in the child) and after the child exited. Rows were read with Node's bundled SQLite 3.53.4 from private copies.

| Scenario | Verified initial state | Result | Rows / migrations | Verbatim helper / mine / old strict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 absent | WAL-mode header, **no `-wal`/`-shm` after the writer process exited**; no fallback copy was needed | exit code 0, `ok Database`, `ok Default model gpt-6.1-terra (codex)`; DB `c749672c…` identical; **`-wal` 0 B + `-shm` created**, also after exit | 12/30, identical; terra not stored | accept / accept / **reject** |
